issues.evidence: ls -la A/ shows an empty directory; probes/results.json A: 0/14 pass; static/A-ruff.txt 'No Python files found'
issues.summary: A has no deliverable: expense_splitter.py is missing, so no requirement is met.

issues.evidence: probe P12_malformed_record_clean_error: '[{"payer":"A"}]' in the data file -> Traceback KeyError: 'amount_cents' at B/expense_splitter.py:87
issues.summary: load() checks only that the data is a list; malformed records crash with a raw traceback instead of a clean error.
There is no upper bound on amounts, so absurd values like 1e400 are accepted and saved.
Exceptions are re-raised inside except blocks without 'from', which loses the exception chaining context.

blinding_guess.why: A is empty and B is one plain file with no spec artifacts, so there is nothing to tell which process produced either.

notes: A/ is an empty directory, so every probe fails on it by construction and all its scores are 0. B uses integer cents with a deterministic leftover-cent split and heap-based greedy largest-debtor/largest-creditor matching, and it writes the file atomically. P01 first failed on both sides because of a bug in my probe (Python 3.9 has no sys.stdlib_module_names). I fixed it with an explicit stdlib allowlist and reran both sides. Bandit reported nothing for B, and neither side ships tests.
